text:
emma: Quick thread  posted a tiny mock for the SLO alert snippet (link: https://img.redwood.test/snippet/card1.png). Need input on 3 quick tradeoffs: 1) show channels as a compact inline list with a +N overflow or show a vertical priority list? 2) suppression tone: 'Muted' vs 'Suppressed' vs 'Silenced'? 3) screen-reader announcement behavior when suppression state flips.

rob: For eyeball scans I like inline with +N, but numeric priority (1,2) beside each channel helps preserve order. If theres a fallback, show it under the list as 'fallback: regional' in muted text.

alia: Accessibility: inline chips are fine only if keyboard focus moves through them predictably and each chip has an aria-label like 'channel: pagerduty priority 1'. If we visually truncate the reason, add an offscreen element with the full text for SRs. Also the suppression token color needs contrast fix.

sam: Announce behavior: use aria-live="polite" for suppression changes and a focused role=status element when the user expands details. For +N use role=button, aria-expanded toggles. For copy, prefer 'Muted until 12:00' for clarity; 'Suppressed' is more technical.

design-bot: Figma frame updated: https://www.figma.com/file/new/snippet-card-v1

emma: Plan: go inline +N with small priority labels, use 'Muted until HH:MM' in UI and full reason in tooltip/offscreen SR text. @alia to post contrast tokens and focus rules, @sam to draft aria snippets, @rob to mock priority numbers in the layout. Sync Wed 10am to sign off. :calendar:
